title: China climate-resilience infrastructure funding trajectory (2022–2026)
executive_question: Is government funding for water conservancy, urban drainage, and disaster prevention on a durable multi-year growth path after the 2026 flood and typhoon season?
required_metrics: China central government disaster prevention and emergency management budget allocation, CNY billion, 2022
China central government disaster prevention and emergency management budget allocation, CNY billion, 2023
China central government disaster prevention and emergency management budget allocation, CNY billion, 2024
China central government disaster prevention and emergency management budget allocation, CNY billion, 2025
China central government disaster prevention and emergency management budget allocation, CNY billion, 2026
China local government special bond issuance for water conservancy and urban drainage, CNY billion, 2022–2026
China National Development and Reform Commission central budget investment in disaster prevention and reduction, CNY billion, 2022–2026
comparison_set: Annual central budget allocation vs. local special bond issuance vs. NDRC central budget investment for disaster prevention, 2022–2026
preferred_sources: Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China budget reports
National Development and Reform Commission annual investment plans
Ministry of Water Resources annual work conferences and budget disclosures
China Government Bond and local special bond issuance data from ChinaBond or Wind
search_queries: 地方政府专项债 水利 城市排水 防灾 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026
国家发展改革委 中央预算内投资 防灾减灾 年度计划
data_quality_rule: Use only official budget documents or bond issuance data with explicit annual figures. If fewer than four same-basis annual observations are found, apply a transparent CAGR or GDP-linked estimation rule, mark intermediate years as estimates, and never present two endpoints as a trend line.
narrative_role: Establishes the funding tailwind that underpins the multi-year order pipeline thesis before segment-level attractiveness is discussed.
pre_exhibit_context: The 2026 disaster response is expected to accelerate government spending, but the investment committee needs evidence that this is a trend, not a one-off emergency supplement.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Central and local disaster-prevention funding has grown at a compound rate that supports a multi-year procurement pipeline, with 2026 showing a step-up tied to post-disaster reconstruction and resilience mandates.

pre_exhibit_context: The document identifies reservoir overtopping and urban flooding as failure modes, but the committee needs evidence that these translate into actual tenders and contracts.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Tender volume and value for water conservancy and drainage projects surged in the months after July 2026, confirming a real procurement wave rather than a policy aspiration.

title: China and UAE catastrophe insurance penetration and flood risk protection gap (2020–2026)
executive_question: Is catastrophe insurance penetration in China and UAE growing fast enough to create a durable climate finance opportunity, or are insurers still in a payout-heavy phase?
required_metrics: China catastrophe insurance premium volume, CNY billion, 2020–2026
China catastrophe insurance penetration rate, percentage of economic losses covered, 2020–2026
UAE catastrophe insurance premium volume, AED billion, 2020–2026
UAE catastrophe insurance penetration rate, percentage of economic losses covered, 2020–2026
China agricultural weather insurance premium volume, CNY billion, 2020–2026
UAE parametric insurance premium volume, AED billion, 2020–2026
comparison_set: China vs. UAE catastrophe insurance premium volume and penetration rate, 2020–2026
preferred_sources: National Financial Regulatory Administration (金融监管总局) insurance statistics
UAE Central Bank insurance sector reports
Swiss Re sigma reports
Munich Re NatCatSERVICE database
search_queries: UAE catastrophe insurance penetration premium 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026
parametric insurance flood UAE premium volume 2020 2026
data_quality_rule: Use only regulatory or reinsurer published annual figures. If penetration rate is not directly published, calculate as insured losses divided by total economic losses from the same source and label as derived. If fewer than four annual observations are available, apply a transparent CAGR from the earliest and latest available years, mark intermediate years as estimates, and never present two endpoints as a trend line.
narrative_role: Tests the insurance and climate finance hypothesis by showing the gap between economic losses and insured losses over time.
pre_exhibit_context: The document notes insurance payout increases after disasters, but the committee needs to see whether penetration is rising structurally or only after major events.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Catastrophe insurance penetration remains low relative to economic losses in both markets, indicating a large protection gap but also confirming that insurers face short-term payout pressure before risk-model and parametric products scale.
